label: verify-t3-lumen-lay

claims.claim: MDCK lumens are often dented (sphericity about 0.3 to 0.7); changing pumping or removing claudins did not strongly change that.
claims.source_says: The sphericity of lumens ranged from Ψ ~ 0.70 to very far from spherical (Ψ ~ 0.3)... modulating fluid pumping via ddAVP or ouabain did not strongly influence lumen shape. Cldn-qKO cells formed lumens whose solidity did not differ from wildtype to a significant degree
claims.note: All three passages found in the Europe PMC full text; the knockout result is stated as not significantly different.

claims.claim: Authors' alternative: each cell makes roughly fixed inner surface, and extra inner surface (Rab11a) makes lumens more dented at the same cell count.
claims.source_says: Rab11a-GFP spheroids generated a significantly larger apical domain and a significantly decreased solidity, compared to wildtype cells with the same number of cells. Average luminal surface area per cell varied only modestly between spheroids of 2 to >8 cells.
claims.note: Both the fixed-area-per-cell observation and the Rab11a effect are in the paper.

claims.claim: The published model was tuned on the data and is a 2-D slice, so a pre-registered frozen-prediction test on unseen details is the real test; blindness is only partial.
claims.source_says: The parameters p and lb were free parameters and tuned to agree with data... it models a two-dimensional cross-section of a three-dimensional object.
claims.note: Tuning and the 2-D limitation are in the source; the pre-registered test and partial blindness are the project's own plan, not the paper.

claims.claim: Law set 1.8.1 has no lumen-shape law; its only related law is the thin-wall Laplace bound, which has no instance.
claims.source_says: A radius, a wall thickness and a wall strength: none exists in this project for any fish, so the bound is proved with no instance.
claims.note: Grep of the registry found no lumen or epithelium law (the 'cyst' hit was 'selenocysteine'); other pressure laws are depth-related, not cavity laws, though I did not read them in full.

overall: All four key claims hold. Three are supported directly by the Vasquez 2021 full text and the local Laplace law file. The third is partly supported, because the pre-registration and partial-blindness parts are the project's plan, not a source statement.
